en: Riu, riu, chiu, the riverbank guard [?],
God kept the wolf from our ewe-lamb.
The raging wolf wanted to bite her,
But mighty God knew how to defend her,
He chose to make her so that she could not sin,
Nor would this virgin have even original sin.
Riu, riu, chiu, the riverbank guard [?],
God kept the wolf from our ewe-lamb.
This one who is born is the great monarch,
Christ the patriarch clothed in flesh.
He has redeemed us by making himself little,
Though he was infinite, he made himself finite.
Riu, riu, chiu, the riverbank guard [?],
God kept the wolf from our ewe-lamb.
This one comes to give life to the dead,
And comes to repair the fall of all;
This little lad is the light of day,
This is the lamb that Saint John spoke of.
Riu, riu, chiu, the riverbank guard [?],
God kept the wolf from our ewe-lamb.
Many prophecies have foretold him,
And even in our days we have lived to see it,
God made man we see on the earth,
And man in heaven, because he willed it.
Riu, riu, chiu, the riverbank guard [?],
God kept the wolf from our ewe-lamb.
Mark well, and let it suit you, that so I heard it [?],
That God could not have made her more than mother;
He who was her Father was born of her today,
And he who created her was called her Son.
Riu, riu, chiu, the riverbank guard [?],
God kept the wolf from our ewe-lamb.
I saw a thousand lads who went about singing.
Flying about here, making a thousand sounds,
Saying to Gascons [?]: Glory be in heaven,
And peace on earth, for Jesus was born.
Riu, riu, chiu, the riverbank guard [?],
God kept the wolf from our ewe-lamb.
Since now we have what we desired,
Let us all go together, let us take gifts;
We will all give him our will,
Since he came to make himself equal with us
Riu, riu, chiu, the riverbank guard [?],
God kept the wolf from our ewe-lamb.
notes: Refrain, line 1: 'Riu, riu, chiu' imitates a bird's call. 'La guarda ribera' is obscure: it may mean 'the guard of the riverbank' or be read as an imperative, 'guard the riverbank'.
Refrain, line 2: literally 'God guarded the wolf from our ewe-lamb'; cordera, a female lamb, stands for the Virgin Mary.
Line 2.3: quízole hazer, 'he willed to make her'.
Line 4.3: the edition prints 'Anos [Ha nos]', 'has us', i.e. 'he has redeemed us'.
Line 6.3: moçuelo (mozuelo), a lad, a young boy.
Line 8.2: lo hemos alcançado, 'we have reached it', i.e. lived to see it.
Line 10.1: the sense of the line is unclear; ansina is an old rustic form of así, 'thus', and oyera may be 'I heard' or 'he heard'.
Line 12.1: garçones, young men or lads; here the angels.
Line 12.3: a gascones, literally 'to Gascons'; the sense of the word here is uncertain.
Line 14.4: the edition has no closing punctuation.
